A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STAF research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite substantial retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original image, audio, shape, inverse-problem, and NeRF experiments, together with computational comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and adds DIV2K results, parameter-dynamics and freezing experiments, audio NTK analysis, and a perceptual-loss experiment.

M1.justification: The Fourier-sum activation, layer-wise sharing, and standard joint optimization remain. Listing 1 changes the amplitude initializer's Laplace scale from 1/(2τ) to 2/τ, aligning the implementation with the existing theory. Appendix G additionally tests an MSE-plus-LPIPS objective as a variant.

E1.justification: The image datasets, Bach audio, Stanford shapes, super-resolution, denoising, and five NeRF scenes remain covered. Replaced illustrative images and additional DIV2K samples stay within existing image-reconstruction coverage; the new analyses introduce no distinct data domain or task.

E2.justification: The Cameraman comparison containing Chebyshev KAN in v2 Figure 3 is removed; KAN remains only in related-work discussion. FINER is added to the activation-map comparison in Figure 2. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include five randomly selected 512×512 DIV2K samples, freezing sinusoidal parameters after 200 of 500 training steps, and comparing MSE with an added LPIPS loss. Existing benchmark settings largely persist. The corrected initializer listing does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.8 adds parameter-update tracking and a freezing control to test the two-phase NTK approximation. C.9 extends empirical NTK analysis to audio, and Appendix G experimentally tests the distortion–perception trade-off. These substantially expand validation beyond the retained component, sharing, capacity, and initialization ablations.

E5.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same plus/minus and variance reporting. v3 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Results are substantially extended and selectively revised. In Figure 4, INCODE changes from 37.21 to 38.80 dB while STAF remains at 40.47 dB, replacing FINER as runner-up. v3 adds five-image DIV2K scores, convergence trajectories, audio NTK findings, and freezing/perceptual-loss outcomes, while removing or replacing earlier illustrative-image results. Most benchmark tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 revises initialization independence assumptions and adds a sine-transform density derivation in Appendix D.1, an exact frequency/amplitude analysis using Jacobi–Anger and Bessel expansions in Appendix E, and an alternative Delannoy asymptotic proof in Appendix F. These are substantive additions beyond relocating the existing Kronecker and NTK theory.

C1.justification: v2 presents a novel activation family with broad SOTA superiority and spectral-bias benefits. v3 recasts STAF as an instantiation of a unified sinusoidal framework, narrows performance claims toward distortion metrics and evaluated settings, and explicitly disclaims eliminating spectral bias or universally dominating baselines.

C2.justification: v3 explains the two-phase NTK model as an approximation, motivates smaller τ for denoising through reduced noise fitting, develops latency-based tuning advice, and specifies applicability boundaries. It also qualifies hash-encoding comparisons and expands the existing perceptual-quality caveat with implications from the new hybrid-loss experiment.

D1.justification: The initialization code is corrected, and Appendix B.2 newly identifies the Tokyo experiment's PyTorch InstantNGP pipeline with activation substitutions. The abstract replaces the direct repository reference with a project-page reference. Most hardware, learning-rate, architecture, and implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts substantially toward organizing an existing sinusoidal family. v3 adds Novello et al. and Fourier Learning Machines, distinguishes input Fourier features, output Fourier architectures, and hidden activations, and reframes KAN as an alternative architecture rather than primarily an inferior comparator.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Expressivity theory precedes experiments, the former appendix NTK discussion enters the main text, and appendices are reorganized into A–G. Some cross-references become malformed, including 'Appendix 5' and '??1'.

P2.justification: Image comparisons are rebuilt with larger crops and convergence panels, Figure 2 changes input and adds FINER, and the Tokyo error-map display gains enlarged regions and a scale. v3 adds Table 6 and Figures 17–18, relocates existing figures, expands captions, and adopts substantially different journal formatting.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's largely asserted two-phase approximation and broad superiority claims, v3 supplies targeted controls, better qualifies conclusions, and corrects the initialization-code mismatch. These improve evidential support and reproducibility. The gain is tempered by errors in added theory: Appendix D.1 Equation 52 integrates to 2/3, rather than 1, when a=3π/4 and b=0. Broken cross-references also reduce clarity.
